results.title: Founder Institute Review (2026): Worth It? | Foundinity
results.content: the complaints we read were about slow or missing replies, unclear steps for dropping out and getting a refund, late organisers and working groups that didn't work. In one detailed one-star review, the reviewer said a refund deadline changed; Founder Institute disputed that in its reply. One reviewer called the cofounder matching weak. [...] 1\. It charges founders. Most accelerators don't charge a fee. A 2012 Hacker News comment by someone who kept a list of seed accelerators said he left Founder Institute off because it charges startups to take part. In a 2015 thread, another commenter objected to it calling itself an accelerator while charging up front. That is a fair objection to the label, not evidence of fraud. 2. You don't get money for joining. You pay Founder Institute a fee; it doesn't pay you. GrowthMentor's review says the programme doesn't provide capital, and that some of the founders it spoke to hadn't expected that. If you join expecting funding, you'll be disappointed. 3. Some people had a bad experience. On Trustpilot, which doesn't verify reviews, the complaints we read were about slow or missing replies, [...] - Support depends on the chapter. The recent Trustpilot complaints about slow replies and late organisers are about specific cohorts. With chapters in many cities run locally, quality is likely to differ by place, so talk to people from the chapter you're considering. Graham Archbold, who joined the London 2019/20 cohort, makes the same point at the start of a Medium post titled "Is Founder Institute a Scam?": it runs as a franchise, so the method is the same everywhere but each cohort's culture depends largely on its local directors. (The rest of his post is for Medium members only, so we haven't used it.)

Dec 16, 2024

Image 50: Rated 1 out of 5 stars

## very Bad Foundit Services
Job Application Process:  
  
The system allows users to apply for jobs that are already expired, causing unnecessary confusion and wasted effort.  
Even when pressing "Confirm and Apply," the application process fails to complete, leaving applicants frustrated.  
Resume Parsing:  
  
The ATS fails to fetch keywords correctly from uploaded resumes, which can negatively impact how recruiters view the application.  
Support and Communication:  
  
Foundit Support representatives often call to ask for money, which is unprofessional and unethical.  
Instead of providing genuine assistance, the focus seems to be on marketing emails rather than resolving user concern
